title: Can the AI industry persuade data center opponents by getting rid of NDAs?
slides: Can data centers win trust by dropping NDAs?
Communities fear hidden water and power costs.
But some operators now publish full environmental data.
You can demand those numbers before any approval vote.
Ask your local operator: will you sign a transparency pledge?
thread_text:
1. The NDA era is ending

Data centers have long hidden their water and power usage behind non-disclosure agreements. Now some operators are voluntarily publishing full environmental data.

2. What they didn't want you to see

Communities near these facilities have been hit with skyrocketing utility bills and drained aquifers. They had no way to prove it until now.

3. A new transparency playbook

A handful of operators are releasing real-time water consumption and energy source data. It's a direct challenge to the industry's default secrecy.

4. Your leverage before the vote

Local approval boards often greenlight projects without hard numbers. You can demand environmental disclosures as a condition before any vote.

5. Ask them this one question

"Will you sign a transparency pledge?" If they hesitate, you have your answer. Ask at the next town hall.
